text:
ConocoPhillips climbed 2.6% today to $137.55, extending a nine-day rally that's now up 9.1%. The driver is oil prices rising sharply on geopolitical tensions: a deadly Saudi airport attack pushed Brent crude above $106, while ongoing conflict in Ukraine and potential U.S. military involvement in Middle East shipping disputes (against Iran-backed Houthis) are keeping energy markets on edge. For an oil and gas producer, higher crude prices directly translate to stronger earnings potential.

The backdrop includes policy uncertainty that's also bullish for the sector. The Trump administration is exploring sanctions relief on Russian energy and military involvement in the Red Sea, both of which could disrupt global supply and keep crude elevated — the kind of geopolitical premium that benefits large-cap producers like ConocoPhillips regardless of U.S. domestic policy outcomes.
